record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: How can agents in a social organization be characterized using topological or temporal-network information? The question should account for the lack of a general way to assign agent importance and for possible proxies such as hierarchy, eigenvector centrality, coreness, weighted k-core centrality, and temporal-network centralities.

evidence.quote: Questions • How can we characterize agents, using topological information?

In each organization, agents have a diﬀerent importance, ri, that reﬂects their hierarchical status, reputation, embedding in the organization, knowledge, etc. To obtain values for ri is a challenge in itself and depends on the available data. Because there is no general solution, we resort to some guiding examples.

artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns a general, principled assignment of agent-importance scores from purely topological/temporal-network data. No universal solution is known: the network-science literature offers many centrality measures (eigenvector, k-core, weighted k-core, temporal centralities), but their comparative merits and an axiomatic characterization remain an active area of research, and no consensus framework has been established. The problem is therefore considered open.

status_evidence.title: Axioms for Centrality
status_evidence.snippet: We investigate the most common centrality measures... none satisfies all of our axioms.
status_evidence.claim: No standard centrality measure satisfies a natural set of axioms simultaneously, indicating the question of a canonical importance measure is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Temporal Networks (Holme & Saramäki)
status_evidence.snippet: Centrality measures for temporal networks generalize static centralities but no unique choice is canonical.
status_evidence.claim: Temporal centralities remain a family of competing proxies with no general solution.
